football_evidence.question: Can Colorado’s pass rush get to Avery Johnson?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Kansas State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 4.6 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.

When Kansas State has the ball (third down): Kansas State’s offense converts 53.5% of its third downs, and Colorado’s defense allows opponents to convert 42.0% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Kansas State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Kansas State’s offense turns 10.1% of its runs into explosive gains, and Colorado’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
When Colorado has the ball (third down): Colorado’s offense converts 32.1% of its third downs, and Kansas State’s defense allows opponents to convert 36.6% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).
contradicting: When Kansas State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Kansas State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.3% of its runs, and Colorado’s defense stops 26.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
